title: One request. 81 backend attempts.

provenance.source: Authored illustrative model for the STE-Pro Max showcase, October 3, 2026

definitions.A: Total attempts per retrying layer per incoming call, including the initial attempt
definitions.L: Number of serial layers before the backend
definitions.layer_i: Layer 1 receives the original request; layer L calls the backend
definitions.attempt_mark: One cumulative downstream call at the indicated boundary, not a simultaneous call
definitions.backend_attempts: Only the final boundary count; not the sum of all boundary counts

assumptions: Every backend attempt fails, and each failure propagates upstream after downstream attempts are exhausted.
All layers are serial and invoke one next layer, or the backend at the final layer.
Every retrying layer exhausts its total attempt budget for each incoming call.
An upstream retry starts the full downstream sequence again with fresh downstream attempt budgets.
There are no shared retry budgets, early exits, deadlines, cancellation, caching, circuit breakers, or deduplication.
In the single-owner comparison, layer 1 has the same attempt budget A; every other layer forwards each incoming call exactly once.
limits: No real network calls, artificial delays, storage, or automatic playback.
No estimate of elapsed time, concurrency, throughput, success probability, or production performance.
Reducing attempt counts is not a resilience guarantee or a production policy recommendation.
